messages:
Aisha: Heads-up: user reported TS error when importing our edge entrypoint in Cloudflare Worker sample: "Cannot find module 'redwood/edge' or its corresponding type declarations." They import like `import { createClient } from 'redwood/edge'`.

Tom: Do we publish an "edge" subpath export? I thought we only had conditional exports for node vs import.

Riley: We added ./edge in exports in last week's draft but didn't wire types. TS resolves types differently: it looks at types or typesVersions and doesn't honor conditional exports for types unless we use typesVersions to map subpaths.

Priya: Exact repro from user: tsserver complains in VSCode, but build (esbuild) works. So runtime is fine, editor/IDE experience broken. This is a big DX friction for onboarding.

Aisha: Confirmed. Quick repro: ```ts
// worker.mts
import { createClient } from 'redwood/edge';
const c = createClient({ token: 'x' });
```
TS: Cannot find module 'redwood/edge' or its corresponding type declarations.

Tom: Two fixes: 1) publish a dist/edge/index.d.ts and add a path in typesVersions that maps the subpath to the d.ts; or 2) add a top-level types file that re-exports edge types (but that leaks node-only types maybe).

Riley: I'd prefer typesVersions mapping so we keep clear boundaries. Example snippet for package.json: ```json
"typesVersions": { "*": { "./edge": ["dist/edge/index.d.ts"], "./edge/*": ["dist/edge/*"] } }
```
That makes tsserver resolve 'redwood/edge'.

Priya: Also watch package exports conditions: bundlers use the "import" condition, but tsserver uses the "types" or typesVersions. We need to keep them in sync. Otherwise devs see different behavior in IDE vs runtime.

Aisha: Another gotcha: some customers import via `redwood/dist/edge` or use path-mapped imports in frameworks. We should document recommended import paths and avoid encouraging deep imports.

Tom: Good point. For the SDK, maybe we should encourage `import from 'redwood/edge'` and add a compatibility file at dist/edge/index.mjs that re-exports from the compiled ESM entry so tooling that walks files still resolves. That plus typesVersions should cover most cases.

Riley: Tests: add a tiny workspace with TS project that runs tsserver in CI (or uses `tsc --noEmit` in a worker-targeted tsconfig) to prevent regressions. I can add a GitHub Action step using Node 18 and the same tsserver version we recommend.

Priya: Also add a short snippet in docs explaining "If you see \"Cannot find module 'redwood/edge'\" in your editor, run: 1) ensure you installed @latest, 2) restart TS server in VSCode, 3) check node_modules/redwood/package.json for typesVersions mapping." That'll help support.

Aisha: Action items: Riley -> PR for typesVersions + dist/edge/*.d.ts; Tom -> add dist/edge re-export ESM file; Priya -> docs blurb + troubleshooting steps; DevEx Bot -> create issue and add tests.

DevEx Bot: Created issue #451: "Edge subpath types: TS editor resolution failures" and added labels: devex, types, edge. Assigned to @Riley. Suggested CI: run `pnpm -w build && pnpm -w -C examples/ts-worker tsc --noEmit` on node 18.

Tom: One more subtle thing: typesVersions only works for TypeScript >= 3.9 (fine) but some users may use older TS in monorepos. We should mention minimum TS version in docs.

Riley: I'll include a fallback declaration file at `dist/edge.d.ts` that re-exports types so even older TS can pick it up via a top-level types entry if needed. That keeps UX smooth.

Priya: Thanks. This should dramatically reduce confusion for new users trying the worker example. I'll update the onboarding checklist to include restarting the TS server and verifying the installed SDK version. :sparkles:

Aisha: Great work. Let's land the PRs early next week so examples don't break for the upcoming demo.

DevEx Bot: Note: linking issue #451 to roadmap ticket DEVEX-22.
